classification.method: expected class from the harness (new $LATEST config -> cold; new published version -> restore; reused environment -> warm), checked against REPORT (Init Duration / Restore Duration / neither)

conclusion: OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive shows a -5% paired warm shift, but the host/noise assessment is mixed, so this run is inconclusive for deployment. Warm REPORT Duration paired by (round, request) on CPU part 0xd40: -5.15% mean over 9 rounds (every round below 0, range -6.49 to -4.17%; 45 cells; exact sign-flip p=0.00391; the control's own split-half noise is at most 3.05%; homogeneous (round, CPU part, request) cells on 0xd40: faster=12, in-band=33, aggregate mixed). Median warm REPORT Duration 605 -> 587 ms. The engine's own timer agrees (-5.14%). Mechanism (measured): process CPU per warm request changes -1.93% and voluntary context switches rise from 370 to 17453 per request, so idle workers now sleep in the barrier instead of spinning. That the freed cycles go to a thread with work is an inference, not measured. Other CPU parts, same direction but too few rounds to test: 0xd0c: -6.3% over 1 round(s) (1 below 0, 0 above), insufficient; 0xd4f: -5.5% over 2 round(s) (2 below 0, 0 above), underpowered. Side effects: cold first request -0.057 s, 95% CI [-0.145, +0.015] (n=[52, 53]); restored first request -0.029 s [-0.071, +0.039] (n=[29, 29]), its inference -27 ms [-38, -6]; cold max memory -2 MB. Passive and spin30k are not distinguishable from each other on 0xd40 (see the spin30k result). Recommendation: do not adopt from this run; rerun the affected comparison with enough within-cell precision to separate the shift from control spread. Correctness: 1439/1439 answers bit-identical to ctl for the same request and CPU part in this run, and 5579/5579 bit-identical to P1's reference where it covers the CPU part. libgomp's own start-up print (OMP_DISPLAY_ENV=VERBOSE) shows GOMP_SPINCOUNT=0 on this arm and 300000 on ctl, so the variable reached the library. Errors in the whole run: 0 function errors and 1 client-side transport error (passive warm, restore leg round 2: SSL EOF after 0.4 s, no REPORT line in the saved logs, so Lambda never ran it); it is published, and carries no answer or latency. Restore rows with client:ReadTimeoutError: 0. Host: CPU parts 0xd40, 0xd0c and 0xd4f as read from /proc/cpuinfo, every comparison is within one part, and no CPU generation is inferred. Warm arms are interleaved pass by pass within each round; cold and restore are sequential arm waves whose order rotates across rounds. Run cost $3.98 (all four arms).

host_variability.method: Every comparison is made within one observed CPU part. Warm (the primary metric): within each round the arms alternate pass by pass (the arm order rotates every pass), so the arms are interleaved within the round, and each (round, request) cell is compared on the same CPU part. Cold and restore waves are sequential arm waves whose position rotates across rounds (a Latin square over 4 rounds): that controls order and round drift but not time-within-round drift. Rows without a CPU part are counted, never compared.

unknown.cgroup: per environment in e13.host.identities; any file the sandbox hides is 'unknown'

hypothesis: P3 attributed 5.7% of warm CPU samples on Lambda to libgomp's spin/barrier code (caller ggml_graph_compute_thread). ggml's barrier is `#pragma omp barrier`, and libgomp's default (OMP_WAIT_POLICY unset) spins 300,000 times before it sleeps on a futex. If that spinning is wasted CPU on a fully used 6-vCPU sandbox (6 OpenMP threads on 6 vCPUs, plus Python's own threads), shortening or removing it makes warm requests up to ~5% faster. Passive waiting may instead add futex wake-up latency at every barrier and slow them. Thread count (6) is not varied.
